D.t: Phil Weiser leads by 19.9 in the forecast and wins 99% of simulations. The cushion is about 563,515 votes; a one point swing is about 14,187 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +10.6 and D +28.7. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Denver, a projected net 228,283 votes; Boulder, a projected net 117,470 votes; Jefferson, a projected net 93,845 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: El Paso, R +3.2, 11.8% of the vote; Douglas, even, 7.1% of the vote; Pueblo, D +0.1, 2.7% of the vote; Garfield, D +8.5, 1.0% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Phil Weiser runs furthest behind in Pueblo, Mesa, Weld. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 82% of voters, 55 to 42, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.09 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 73% of voters, 59 to 38, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.67 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 61% of voters, 58 to 38, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.04 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Phil Weiser: Immigration voters 21 to 76, Small counties 45 to 51, Midsize counties 48 to 48. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$725K cash against $158K. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.
Registered Democrats cast 32% of the 1,174,321 ballots in Colorado so far, against 24% for the other party. That is 4.2 points better for Democrats than the forecast expected by now.

D.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.5 points toward Phil Weiser. Bank it: chase the remaining mail ballots and low propensity voters who have not voted.
